QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_14

question.text: In the Indian forex market, what is the settlement convention for a 'spot' transaction?

answer.text: Settlement on the second business day after the trade date (T+2)
Settlement on the same day as the trade date (T+0)
Settlement on the next business day (T+1)
Settlement on the third business day (T+3)

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series I page 28 lays out the standard forex settlement conventions: cash settles on the trade date (T+0), tom on the next business day (T+1), and spot on the second business day after the trade date (T+2), subject to both centres being open. So the spot value date in forex is T+2. The Trap: T+0 is cash and T+1 is tom — both are non-spot conventions. T+3 is not the standard spot date in the forex market. Only the second-business-day rule matches the source definition of spot. Note: Settlement conventions in other markets (equity T+1, commodity settlement) and cross-market arbitrage are not covered in the pages checked and are intentionally not used in this explanation.
